- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.3) after a recent peak, model should not overshoot downward — cap decline to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in true values, adjust forecast to slightly under-predict next peak.  
- Overshoot correction: if model predicts >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price has been volatile, assume mean reversion toward 10–15% below recent high.  
- Lag correction: if true outcome lags forecast by 2–3 days, adjust forecast to be 2–3 days behind the actual trend, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
